data.title: Impact of Bond Market Rout on FX Looks Modest For Now — Market Talk
data.description: Spillovers from rising global government bond yields into the foreign exchange market have been modest so far, MUFG Bank's Lee Hardman says in a note. This is highlighted by low measures of volatility in the forex market, he says. However, the Australian dollar, New Zealand dollar, Swedish krona and emerging markets currencies have underperformed. "Downside risks for those currencies would intensify if rising bond yields and energy prices triggered a deeper correction lower for risk assets heading into year end," he says. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

data.title: European Chip Stocks Mixed After Monday Rout — Market Talk
data.description: Shares of European semiconductor companies are mixed after a Monday selloff that was triggered by calls for a slowdown in the development of advanced artificial-intelligence models over safety concerns. Such calls weighed on global chip stocks on Monday as investors worried that slower AI development could weigh on semiconductor demand. On Tuesday, shares of Dutch semiconductor-equipment maker ASML Holding and smaller rival ASM International are up 0.4% and 0.3%, respectively. BE Semiconductor Industries, the Dutch supplier of semiconductor assembly equipment, is up 0.4%. German chip maker Infineon Technologies declined 0.6%. STMicroelectronics shares fell 0.7%. (mauro.orru@wsj.com)

data.title: Tata Chemicals lead Tata Group rally amid Tata Sons listing prospects
data.description:
Tata Group stocks witnessed strong buying interest on Tuesday after the RBI rejected Tata Sons’ application to deregister as a non-bank lender, reviving prospects of a stock market listing for the holding company.

Tata Consultancy Services, Tata Chemicals, Tata Investment Corporation, TMPV, Tata Motors, Tata Elxsi and other Tata Group stocks traded in the green on Tuesday following the RBI decision.

Among top movers, heavyweigt IT major TCS rose 5.4 per cent to ₹2,322.5 on the BSE, while Tata Chemicals locked in the upper circuit of ₹734.50, up 20 per cent from its previous close of ₹612.10. Tata Investment Corporation rallied 15.2 per cent to ₹750.30.

The potential listing of Tata Sons could improve valuation and unlock value for Tata-linked companies. Tata Chemicals, Tata Motors and Tata Investment Corporation are among the listed Tata companies that own stakes in Tata Sons.

Tata Sons is classified as a core investment company and is subject to RBI rules for non-bank lenders that require companies with assets exceeding ₹1 trillion, or those with direct or indirect access to public funds, to be listed.

RBI’s rejection of Tata Sons’ application to deregister as a non-bank lender has therefore revived prospects of a stock market listing for the holding company.

data.title: Mahindra Manulife Life Insurance appoints Ruchika Varma as Chief Marketing & Customer Officer
data.description:
Mahindra Manulife Life Insurance has appointed Ruchika Malhan Varma as its Chief Marketing and Customer Officer (CMCO), as the company sets out to create a differentiated, AI-driven, digitally enabled and customer-centric life insurance franchise in India.

With over 25 years of experience across financial services, media, entertainment, travel and consumer businesses in India and Asia, Varma brings extensive expertise in brand building, digital transformation, customer experience and business-led marketing, the insurance company said in a release on Tuesday.

At Mahindra Manulife Insurance, Varma will spearhead brand and marketing communications, corporate communications, digital and growth marketing, customer experience, digital experience, partnerships, DEI, sustainability and AI enablement, with a focus on building a consumer-first franchise.

Commenting on her appointment, Suresh Agarwal, MD and CEO, Mahindra Manulife Life Insurance, said, “Ruchika’s experience at the intersection of brand, customer, technology and business makes her an important addition as we set out to build Mahindra Manulife Insurance. Our ambition is to create an AI-first, consumer-driven insurance company that understands customers better, designs simple and effective experiences and delivers relevant protection solutions.”

Varma’s leadership will be instrumental in translating that ambition into a differentiated customer proposition and a strong, trusted brand, Agarwal said.

Sharing her vision for the new role, Varma said, “Insurance is entering a new era where AI, data and deep consumer understanding can fundamentally reshape how customers discover, buy and experience insurance. I am excited to be part of the journey of building Mahindra Manulife Life Insurance as an AI-first, consumer-driven organisation that combines technology and human insight to make insurance more relevant, intuitive and accessible for customers across India.”

Prior to joining Mahindra Manulife, Varma served as the Chief Marketing, Customer and Impact Officer at Generali Central Insurance, leading brand and marketing communications, digital marketing, corporate communications, product strategy and innovation, customer experience, digital acquisition, web sales and telesales, alongside the organisation’s CSR, DEI and sustainability agendas.

Earlier, as Chief Marketing Officer at IDFC FIRST Bank, she played a pivotal role in building and strengthening the IDFC Bank and IDFC FIRST Bank brands. She has also held leadership positions with BBC Worldwide, Lonely Planet, Singapore Tourism Board, VIP Luggage and Electrolux.

“The Mahindra-Manulife JV aims to offer long-term savings and protection solutions tailored to the diverse and growing needs of India’s population, in line with India’s “Insurance for All” vision by 2047. Combining Mahindra’s deep access and extensive distribution in rural and semi-urban areas with Manulife’s proven quality agency, product development and underwriting capabilities catered to urban customers, the joint venture will create long-term value by driving customer centricity and leveraging new technologies,” the release added.

data.title: India consults banks, payment firms on fees for large UPI payments, sources say
data.description:
India's payments authority
is talking to lenders and payments firms on Tuesday to discuss
levying charges on ‌large transactions in the world's largest
retail fast-payment system, three sources familiar with the
plans told Reuters.

The consultations ‌come after India changed its payments
legislation on Monday, ‌allowing ⁠firms to charge transactions of
more than ₹2,000. ⁠All payments using the
Unified Payments Interface have been free so far.

The move will benefit banks and payment firms in Asia's
third-largest economy that posted ​24 billion UPI payments
totalling $311 ‌billion in August.

The agenda for Tuesday's meeting includes the overall fees
to be levied on payments to merchants and the split between
banks, payment apps and aggregators, two of ‌the three sources
said.

Regulatory authorities, including the National Payments
Corporation ​of India and the Reserve Bank of India, are leaning
towards a 0.4 per cent charge but the final ⁠rate and the split have yet
to be decided, the third source said.

The second of the three sources said the ‌banks could get 40 per cent
of the fees, with the remainder evenly divided between the
payment app and the merchant payment services provider.

While person-to-merchant transactions are expected to be
monetized, peer-to-peer transactions will remain free, the
sources said.

All the sources requested anonymity as they are not
authorized to speak to the media. ‌The NPCI and RBI did not
immediately respond to emails seeking comment.

Inching closer

Introduction of charges on UPI would benefit Paytm
and Pine Labs, open an additional revenue source for
banks ⁠and boost prospects for IPO-bound PhonePe and Razorpay.

Analysts at Jefferies ⁠estimate that the fees could generate ₹50 billion to ₹100 billion annually for the
payments industry.

India's payments ‌landscape is dominated by apps that have
received sizeable overseas investment such as Walmart-backed
PhonePe, Alphabet's Google Pay, Paytm ​and
Meta-backed CRED.

data.title: China, HK stocks end lower on weak economic data
data.description:
China and Hong Kong stocks fell on Tuesday, as a mild rebound in AI hardware shares failed to offset losses elsewhere, with mixed August data pointing to persistently weak domestic demand.

** China's blue-chip CSI300 Index ended 0.7% lower, while the Shanghai Composite Index lost 0.5%. Hong Kong benchmark Hang Seng was down 1%.

** China's industrial output picked up pace in August, though sluggish consumption and a worsening investment slump reinforced concerns over deepening economic imbalances.

** Meanwhile, new home prices fell again in August, underscoring persistent weakness in the housing market.

** The CSI 300 Financial and Real Estate Index fell around 1% each, while consumer staple shares lost 0.6%.

** "Following weaker​-​than​-​expected credit demand, August activity data reinforced our view that a recovery in domestic demand remains elusive," Barclays analysts said in a note, adding that they maintain their below​-​consensus 2026 GDP growth forecast of 4.5%.

** The tech-focused STAR50 Index rose as much as 3%, rebounding for the first time in a week from a 4-1/2-month low. The CSI Semiconductor Material and Equipment Thematic Index (.CSI931743) gained 3.2%.

** Onshore sentiment has weakened over the past month, after investors took profits from a record-breaking AI-led rally earlier this year. Liquidity has also dried up. Daily turnover of onshore shares hovered near the lowest level since April over the past week.

** Tech majors listed in Hong Kong lost 0.6%, with Tencent up nearly 2%.

** Shares of Guangdong Tianyu Semiconductor jumped more than 7% on the company's share buyback plan.

data.title: Kuwait issues advisory services RFP for Sabah Al-Ahmad elderly care resort PPP
data.description:
By Majda Muhsen

Kuwait has issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) for transaction advisory services for the planned Sabah Al-Ahmad Resort for Elderly Care and Rehabilitation, which is being developed as a public-private partnership (PPP) project.

The Kuwait Authority for Partnership Projects (KAPP) in collaboration with the Ministry of Social Affairs issued the RFP, with companies invited to submit bids by 8 December, local English language news portal The Times Kuwait reported on Tuesday.

Previous reports by The Times Kuwait and other local media have indicated that the resort will be developed on a 133,000-square-metre (sqm) plot within Sabah Al-Ahmad Residential City. In January 2025, the news portal had quoted a ministry official as saying that if the project's final cost exceeded 60 million Kuwaiti dinars ($194.4 million), it would be offered for public subscription.

According to the January 2025 report, the development is planned as an integrated elderly care and rehabilitation facility providing healthcare, social, psychological and recreational services. It will include a five-star hotel, shelter care facility and an awareness centre for Alzheimer's, neurodegenerative diseases and multiple sclerosis.

Other planned facilities include health club; physiotherapy centre; swimming pools for rehabilitation and hydrotherapy; acoustic therapy facilities; playgrounds; walking track; rest areas; restaurant complex; cinema and mosque, as well as administration and supporting facilities.

Earlier plans envisaged an implementation period of approximately three years, from June 2025 to May 2028.

(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)

data.description:

  • Oil prices rise 2%

Major European stock indexes are weak on Tuesday as elevated energy prices and rising bond yields continued to weigh.

The pan-continental STOXX 600 is down 1%, adding to a 0.5% drop on Monday. Major bourses in Frankfurt , Paris and London CURRENCYCOM:UK100 are down between 0.9% and 1%.

Broadly, focus is on the ongoing energy supply disruptions in the Middle East and stalled talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to maritime traffic.

That has pushed oil prices higher and helped global bond yields reach fresh multi-year highs on Tuesday, as markets price in further tightening from global central banks.

Banks (.SX7P) tend to benefit from higher yields but are actually the weak spot in Europe, hindered by comments from Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan after he said sales and trading revenue will be flat in the third quarter.

data.title: German spot power prices rise with solar output set to fall
data.description:
The German spot energy prices rose on Tuesday as solar power production was set to fall.

  • The German day-ahead baseload contract (TRDEBD1) was up by 6.7% to €186 ($214) per megawatt-hour at 0648 GMT, according to LSEG data.

  • Solar power was expected to fall by 2.5 gigawatts to 12.7 GW and wind power to rise by 2.2 GW to 13.4 GW, with consumption expected to edge up by 0.7 GW to 54.7 GW.

  • The equivalent French contract (TRFRBD1) was up 2.4% to €185/MWh, according to LSEG data.

  • Wind power was expected to rise by 1.6 GW in France, while solar power generation was set to fall by nearly 1 GW. Consumption, on the other hand, was seen edging 0.4 GW lower.

  • "Strong wind should weigh on spot prices into the weekend, but the subsequent wind drop and persistently low hydro create upward pressure from Monday September 21st," analysts at Engie's EnergyScan wrote.

  • French nuclear availability rose by 7 percentage points to 80% of total capacity.

  • EDF's St. Alban plant will reduce power output at its two reactors by 2.2 GW on Wednesday due to environmental constraints, the French utility said.

  • Tuesday's strike has cut French electricity supply by 6.7 GW, data from EDF showed. That equals about 15% of total power demand in the early hours, but does not affect the country's status as a net exporter, data from grid operator RTE showed.

  • On a year-ahead basis, neither the French (TRFRBYc1) nor the German (TRDEBYc1) contracts were trading, according to LSEG data.

  • The European carbon market's benchmark contract fell 0.5% to €87.53 a metric ton.

($1 = 0.8675 euros)

data.title: Hyundai Bayon SUV launch expected this Diwali: Price, engine, CNG option, features
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 15 -- Hyundai Motor India on Monday announced the name of its new SUV that will be launched in the Indian market. The new model, Hyundai Bayon, will be positioned between the Venue and Creta in Hyundai's SUV lineup. The company says the name is inspired by Bayonne, a city in France's Basque Country.

The India-spec Bayon will have different specs from the Bayon sold in Europe and Central Asia. The new SUV has already been road-tested by Hyundai, and images have now surfaced offering a glimpse of the car's exterior and cabin. The SUV is expected to make its market debut during the upcoming festive season.

The Bayon is expected to adopt a crossover-inspired design rather than the upright shape seen on some traditional SUVs. The test cars have shown a split-headlamp design that incorporates a full-width LED light bar above the main lights. The lower headlamps on the Hyundai Verna appear to be the same as those on the car, according to Autocar India.

The rising window line, the noticeable kink in the C-pillar area, the roof rails and the flared wheel arches are the key features of the SUV. The rear of the test mules has a thin LED light bar and a prominent roof spoiler.

The cabin has also been spotted for the first time. It seems to have a two-screen dashboard design. These could be 12.3-inch screens like those found on higher-spec versions of the latest Venue. The two-tone steering wheel with Hyundai's Morse code-inspired 'H' is also noticeable.

The Hyundai Bayon is expected to use Creta's 1.5-litre naturally aspirated four-cylinder petrol engine, which produces 115 hp. As previously reported, the engine might be available with a 6-speed manual and a CVT gearbox.

It is expected that a CNG version will also be included in the Bayon range. Another option for the CNG system is an underbody tank, but Hyundai hasn't revealed details of this version yet. The Bayon would be the first model over four metres to get a factory CNG powertrain from Hyundai.

The new model SUV will likely be priced lower than the Creta, with an estimated ex-showroom price of Rs.9 lakh to Rs.14 lakh. This would allow it to sit higher than the Venue and have space between the two SUVs in Hyundai's line-up.

Hyundai has not yet announced the Bayon's exact launch date, prices or complete specifications. More details are expected to be revealed closer to its market introduction. data.title: IT behemoth Infosys shares surge 6%; how Anthropic AI pace warning triggered the rally
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 15 -- Infosys share price surged around 6% in trade on Tuesday, September 15, even as a fresh debate over the pace and safety of frontier artificial intelligence development unfolded globally. The move came after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower pace of AI development, cITing growing safety risks. The head of the AI company also called for the development of AI models to be closely monitored.

Amodei's comments have added to a broader discussion within the AI industry over how quickly the Technology should advance. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and other major AI leaders have also backed a more cautious approach.

The debate has already affected global AI stocks. Nvidia fell 3.4% and SoftBank dropped 10.7% on Monday.

In an online essay, Amodei said the development of AI itself was not in question, but described the associated risks as "serious". He argued that companies and governments need sufficient time to address those risks.

The CEOs of rival AI firms, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk, have both said they agree with Amodei.

The broader Indian IT sector also witnessed strong gains. The NIFTY IT index jumped 5% to 30,390.70, with all 10 constituents trading in the green.

Among individual stocks other than Infosys, TCS traded 5.13% higher at Rs.2,313.70. HCL Technologies shares gained around 6.5% to Rs.1,283.70 apiece on the NSE, while Wipro rose 3.30% to Rs.172.93. Tech Mahindra shares were trading 5.63% higher at Rs.1,627.70 apiece on the NSE.

data.title: Japanese land prices rise for a fifth year
data.description:
Japanese land prices rose 1.5% in the year to July 1, marking a fifth straight year of gains and maintaining the strongest pace of growth since the aftermath of the country's asset-price bubble more than three decades ago, data showed on Tuesday.

While the Bank of Japan has said it sees little sign of overheating in asset prices, the survey will likely be among factors it will scrutinise in determining how swiftly it should dial back stimulus and raise still-low interest rates.

The increase matched last year's rise, which was the largest since a 3.1% gain in 1991, when property prices and the economy were beginning to lose steam after years of red-hot growth.

The data suggests Japan's land market remains supported by a gradual economic recovery, with residential and commercial property prices continuing to rise across much of the country.

Average land prices across the Tokyo, Osaka and Nagoya metropolitan areas rose 4.4% from a year earlier, up 0.1 percentage point from the previous year, the data showed.

Tourist destinations continued to benefit from a surge in inbound visitors. Hakuba, located in Nagano Prefecture, saw commercial land prices jump 35.6% reflecting strong demand in the popular alpine tourist destination.

data.title: Indonesia's Finance Minister Pick Could Be Tonic Markets Want
data.description:
By Amanda Lee and Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

Indonesia has appointed its third finance minister in under two years. That shouldn't inspire much confidence, but analysts say the experienced technocrat could be an antidote for worries about erratic policymaking.

Suahasil Nazara steps into the role with a solid track record. A seasoned economist, he spent almost seven years as deputy finance minister, including under Sri Mulyani Indrawati, the respected former finance minister whose ouster in late 2025 was one of the catalysts that contributed to Indonesian markets' loss of credibility.

He inherits a challenging position: Keeping the budget deficit below the 3% legal ceiling while balancing expansive social programs such as the government's flagship free-meals program.

External headwinds abound too. Drawn-out fighting in the Middle East is keeping energy prices high, heaping pressure on the oil-sensitive rupiah, threatening to swell Indonesia's import bill and adding fiscal strain.

A sustained rise in oil prices could bring Indonesia's fuel subsidy bill to as much as 1.1% of gross domestic product, necessitating expenditure cuts, OCBC economists Lavanya Venkateswaran and Ahmad A Enver said.

Then there's the crisis of confidence among foreign investors. Indonesia's assets have fallen out of favor this year as ratings companies and index providers flagged issues around transparency and investability.

Still, analysts say Suahasil has a shot at winning back investor and institutional confidence.

The initial market reaction to President Prabowo Subianto's announcement Monday signaled cautious optimism, with the Jakarta Composite Index erasing most of its session losses to end the day 0.1% lower.

Whether sentiment firms will depend on whether the new finance minister can communicate more convincingly than his predecessor, Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa, who was in the role for about a year.

Purbaya's tenure was marked by conflicting messages on fiscal policy, crucially over the commitment to keep the budget deficit under 3.0% of gross domestic product, said Capital Economics' Gareth Leather.

Suahasil will need to be much clearer about his priorities and provide investors with more consistent signals on fiscal policy, Leather said.

Execution will be key too.

OCBC thinks respecting the 3.0% limit seems manageable as the deficit is tracking at about 2.7% of GDP.

Still, Suahasil has his work cut out for him in navigating cash-intensive government programs and new policies including an initiative to manage commodity exports.

Economists at Citi don't expect to see a change in the political directions of flagship programs such as free meals and infrastructure. But management could change.

Suahasil, who has a doctorate from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, has been consistent in his priorities: quality of spending over headline expansion, tax administration over rate increases, and adherence to the deficit ceiling, Citi said.

"We expect tighter control of social spending leakage and greater use of state financial institutions to mobilize private capital for infrastructure, rather than balance-sheet expansion at the center," Citi's Ferry Wong said.

Stock-exchange reforms to address concerns brought up by index providers have been taken as a positive step toward a market turnaround. A similar investor-friendly pivot at the finance ministry could be the next trigger for putting Indonesia back in investors' good books.

Write to Amanda Lee at amanda.lee@wsj.com and Fabiana Negrin Ochoa at fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com

data.title: India consults banks, payment firms on fees for large UPI payments, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Meeting follows change in law that paves way for charge on large UPI payments
  • Regulators lean toward 0.4% charge, one source says
  • Transactions between individuals to remain free, sources say
  • Jefferies estimates merchant fees could generate 50 billion to 100 billion rupees in annual revenue

By Jaspreet Kalra and Ashwin Manikandan

India's payments authority is talking to lenders and payments firms on Tuesday to discuss levying charges on large transactions in the world's largest retail fast-payment system, three sources familiar with the plans told Reuters.

The consultations come after India changed its payments legislation on Monday, allowing firms to charge transactions of more than 2,000 rupees (about $20). All payments using the Unified Payments Interface have been free so far.

The move will benefit banks and payment firms in Asia's third-largest economy that posted 24 billion UPI payments totalling $311 billion in August.

The agenda for Tuesday's meeting includes the overall fees to be levied on payments to merchants and the split between banks, payment apps and aggregators, two of the three sources said.

Regulatory authorities, including the National Payments Corporation of India and the Reserve Bank of India, are leaning towards a 0.4% charge but the final rate and the split have yet to be decided, the third source said.

The second of the three sources said the banks could get 40% of the fees, with the remainder evenly divided between the payment app and the merchant payment services provider.

While person-to-merchant transactions are expected to be monetized, peer-to-peer transactions will remain free, the sources said.

All the sources requested anonymity as they are not authorized to speak to the media. The NPCI and RBI did not immediately respond to emails seeking comment.

INCHING CLOSER

Introduction of charges on UPI would benefit Paytm and Pine Labs , open an additional revenue source for banks and boost prospects for IPO-bound PhonePe and Razorpay.

Analysts at Jefferies estimate that the fees could generate 50 billion rupees to 100 billion rupees annually for the payments ​industry.

India's payments landscape is dominated by apps that have received sizeable overseas investment such as Walmart-backed PhonePe (PHOP.NS), Alphabet's Google Pay, Paytm and Meta-backed CRED.

($1 = 95.8675 Indian rupees)

data.title: U.S. 10-Year Treasury Yield Rises to Highest Since 2007
data.description:
By Emese Bartha

The selloff in global bonds gained traction on Tuesday, pushing the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield to its highest level since 2007 after it rose above 5% for the first time in almost three years on Monday.

The 10-year Treasury yield hit a high of 5.041%, Tradeweb data showed, as heightened tensions in the Middle East fueled concerns over energy prices and inflation, leaving a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike on Wednesday looking close to certain.

"Rates markets remain hostage to oil and geopolitics ahead of Wednesday's Federal Open Market Committee [meeting]," Evelyne Gomez-Liechti, multiasset strategist at Mizuho said in a note.

Any brief optimism around Iran diplomacy on Monday proved short-lived and U.S. Treasurys were then sold as oil prices began to rise again.

Write to Emese Bartha at emese.bartha@wsj.com
